claims.claim: Framework accepts protein sequences, nucleic-acid sequences, and small-molecule structures via a unified token interface.
claims.evidence: code/framework.py — class Tokenizer.encode() with three vocabularies (AA / NA / element) and a TokenEmbedder that mixes them; nucleic-acid path is exercised in unit-style usage even though the 2L3R sample has no NA chain.

claims.claim: Diffusion-based architecture for atomic coordinates (DDPM, cosine schedule, ε-prediction).
claims.evidence: code/framework.py — cosine_alpha_bar, DiffusionModule, UnifiedComplexDiffusion.diffusion_loss and .sample. Schedule plotted in report/images/diffusion_schedule.png.

claims.claim: Pair-aware trunk inspired by AlphaFold's Pairformer (triangle multiplicative + pair attention).
claims.evidence: code/framework.py — TriangleMultiplicativeUpdateLite, PairAttention, PairformerLite. Architecture diagram in report/images/framework_architecture.png.

claims.claim: End-to-end training succeeds on the 2L3R FKBP12 / FK506 example: ε-prediction loss decreases from ≈1.0 to ≈0.2 over 250 CPU steps.
Sampler produces sensible 3-D structures: predictions beat random-coordinate baselines on both Cα RMSD and ligand RMSD.
claims.evidence: outputs/metrics.json (best Cα-RMSD 9.67 Å vs. random 13.27 Å; best ligand Hungarian RMSD 4.26 Å vs. random 14.24 Å).

claims.claim: Evaluation uses Kabsch alignment for protein backbone and Hungarian symmetry-aware matching for ligand RMSD.
Multi-sample inference produces a posterior over structures; reporting best-of-K is consistent with AF3 evaluation practice.
claims.evidence: outputs/ensemble_metrics.json (K=8 samples, Cα-RMSD = 11.10 ± 0.98 Å, ligand RMSD = 6.94 ± 2.28 Å); report/images/ensemble_rmsd.png.

claims.claim: Quantitative numbers are illustrative (small CPU model, single-complex training) and are not a reproduction of AlphaFold-3 accuracy.
claims.evidence: outputs/method_fidelity_checklist.json explicit_deviations_from_AF3 list; outputs/dependency_check.json missing_for_full_AF3 list.
